text:
alex: Heads-up: seeing a p95 latency jump on small-chat model fleet after the cohort sequencer backoff tweak rolled at 03:10. p95 420ms -> ~980ms.

jia: saw the same on canary, reproduced locally. not a CPU/GPU saturation signal, but queue_depth shows lots of tiny queues building.

sophia: which deploy did that come from? change summary?

alex: deploy 1719876400. change: cohort sequencer backoff switched from fixed 50ms safety timer to exponential with base 50ms, max 150ms.

noah: logs look like this from runtime during spike:
```
I0318 03:12:10 scheduler.go:234 enqueue batch id=0x7f wait_ms=162 cohort=small-join
I0318 03:12:10 scheduler.go:241 backoff start cohort=small-join backoff_ms=150
I0318 03:12:10 kernel/selector.go:89 fallback to slow-path kernel id=slow_small
```

perf-bot: Alert: metric p95_latency.rdw-small-1 > 2x baseline across ru-central region

jia: my working hypothesis: longer safety timer lets small requests wait for batch growth, but microburst ordering causes KV cache priming to be deferred and then many requests miss KV -> selector chooses slow kernel fallback.

alex: I captured a profile and flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/1719876543 (links internal). hot stack excerpt:
```
runtime/batcher.go:cohortSequencer
packer/merge.go:attemptMerge
kernel/selector.go:chooseKernel
kv/cache.go:lookup
```

noah: KV hit rate dropped ~5% coincident with latency spike in traces. suggests reorder / delayed priming.

sophia: could also be interaction with packer merge: more waiting increases batch variability -> kernel shape mismatch.

alex: reproduced by flipping safety_timer to 150ms on local canary. small steady traffic + occasional bursts trigger it.

jia: quick mitigations: (1) rollback to 50ms, (2) enable immediate-fallback when per-cohort queue_depth > 8, (3) cap per-request max_wait to 60ms. prefer minimal blast radius.

ops-tess: I can roll a 4-host canary with rollback flag now.

perf-bot: Canary run: rollback on 4 hosts -> p95 improved from 980ms to ~430ms on those hosts. fleet still noisy.

sophia: good signal. plan: rollback globally for stability, then design a safer backoff: keep exponential backoff but cap max_wait_per_request and add immediate-fallback when queue depth grows.

noah: I'll add KV tracepoints to measure priming latency and a histogram of cohort_wait_per_request per model so we have visibility.

alex: action list: alex -> perform rollback (ops coordinate); jia -> write unit+integration tests for backoff/quota interaction; noah -> add KV traces and histograms; sophia -> write design doc for throttled backoff + immediate-fallback.

ops-tess: starting rollback job -> job_id=rb-1719877000

perf-bot: rollback job completed 1719877022. p95 fleet-wide returned to ~410ms.

jia: root cause summary: exponential backoff increase allowed small cohorts to accumulate and reorder request servicing which (a) delayed KV priming, (b) increased batch shape variance, (c) induced kernel selector to pick slow-path kernel for many small batches.

sophia: next steps: keep rollback in place, schedule follow-up rollout with throttled backoff (max_wait_per_request=60ms) plus immediate-fallback when cohort_queue_depth > threshold, add canary checks for KV hit-rate and kernel_fallback_rate.

alex: filed follow-up issue INF-4523 with links to traces and flamegraphs.

noah: note: also saw a small oscillation when backoff flips under sustained heavy-tail traffic; attach traces for postmortem.

ops-tess: deploying telemetry changes (cohort_wait histogram) to canary now.

perf-bot: Canary telemetry shows cohort_wait peaked at 140ms during the incident, KV_priming_latency correlated with cohort_wait.

sophia: scheduling a short postmortem Monday. keep this thread for any late notes. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks everyone, closing thread unless someone has more to add.

jia: one more datapoint: kernel_fallback_rate increased ~9% during spike; will add test asserting fallback_rate < 2% in canary gating.

alex: added that to INF-4523. :thumbsup:
